position_in_era.historical_role: The 1997 Ry Cooder–Juan de Marcos González project that returned aging Cuban son players (Compay Segundo, Ibrahim Ferrer, Rubén González, Eliades Ochoa, Omara Portuondo) to international visibility. **Critical bridge to the user's red-heart cluster** (Buena Vista Social Club hits 2023-08–2024-01, plus Ibrahim Ferrer solo) — supplies the pre-existing Cuban-son ear that *Lágrimas Negras* (2003) translates flamenco into. Connects the Orobroy episode to the listener's longest-running Latin lineage.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Recorded March 1996 at EGREM Studios, Havana, in seven days. Produced by Ry Cooder for World Circuit. Released 1997. Won 1998 Grammy for Best Tropical Latin Performance; over 8 million copies sold.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Compay Segundo, Ibrahim Ferrer, Rubén González, Eliades Ochoa, Omara Portuondo — most over 70 at recording. Juan de Marcos González as Cuban side-organizer.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Havana, EGREM Studios — formerly RCA Cuba's recording facility, with retained 1950s acoustics.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Tres, guitar, bongos, bass, piano, voice — classical Cuban son ensemble.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Cultural watershed; reactivated international interest in Cuban traditional music for a decade.
